subject: gk
question: Which Article of the Constitution defines Advocate General as the legal advisor to a State Government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 165**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 165 of the Indian Constitution specifies the role of the Advocate General as the legal advisor to the State Government.
 
• The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor of the respective state.
 
• The Advocate General must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.
 
• The Advocate General's duty is to advise the state government on legal matters and to perform other legal duties assigned by the Governor.
 
• The Advocate General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both the houses of the state legislature but without the right to vote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 166**

 
 
• It deals with the conduct of business of the government of a state and the orders and instruments made and executed in the name of the Governor.
 
 
 
• **Article 164**
 
 
• It pertains to the appointment of Chief Minister and other ministers and the tenure of their office in the state government.
 
 
 
• **Article 167**
 
 
• It outlines the duties of the Chief Minister with regard to furnishing information to the Governor and to communicate decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of state affairs and proposals for legislation.
